predecessors.name: Lombards
predecessors.text: the Lombard conquests in central Italy: infobox 'Preceded by: Kingdom of the Lombards'; origins 'traditionally placed during the reign of Alboin, around 571', or after the 575-576 Byzantine offensive…

successors.name: Kingdom of Italy (medieval)
successors.text: Lambert's realm (the Kingdom of Italy except the Adda-Po territory, plus the duchy) passes to Berengar, who 'had taken Pavia' within days of Lambert's death; Cliopatria's 899 Kingdom of Italy shape…

ledger.x: 571: the Lombard duchy of Spoleto arises under Faroald I.
741: Cliopatria's shape grows from 15.8k to 22.8k km2 and is cut out of the Lombard kingdom's shape.
751: 'In the late spring or summer 751, Aistulf placed Spoleto under his direct control without naming a replacement duke'.
759: Spoleto and Benevento rebel while Desiderius is in the Roman Campagna; Gisulf is elected duke about 759 or 760 and Theodicius about 763.
776: 'In 776, two years after the fall of Pavia, Spoleto fell likewise to Charlemagne.'
778: mirror of the duchy-of-benevento ledger (loss 778, confidence 1).
788 or 789: the Lombard duke Hildeprand drops out of the record and Charlemagne appoints the Frank Winigis.
842: the infobox dates the duchy's 'resurrection as a Frankish margraviate'; Guy I, a Frank, is recorded as duke in 845.
877: Lambert I of Spoleto seizes Rome.
883: Guy III unites Camerino with Spoleto.
896: Lambert and Berengar partition the kingdom near Pavia.
15 October 898: Lambert dies, 'killed near Marengo', and 'within days, Berengar had taken Pavia'; the Spoleto page has Lambert II 'killed by count Hugh' in 898.

wars.name: Byzantine offensive of 575-576
wars.outcome: The Spoleto page offers the offensive under Baduarius as the context for the duchy's rise under Faroald I; no border is dated.

wars.name: Faroald II's seizure of Classis
wars.outcome: Faroald II captured Classis; King Liutprand made him restore it.

wars.name: Liutprand and Transamund II of Spoleto
wars.outcome: Transamund submitted to Liutprand in 729 and gave hostages; in 740 he invaded, killed Hilderic and reclaimed power, and Liutprand then granted the duchy to Agiprand.

wars.name: Desiderius's invasion of Spoleto
wars.outcome: The duchy was vacant for two years after the invasion of 757-758 and rebelled in 759 together with Benevento.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Lombard kingdom
wars.outcome: Charlemagne conquered the kingdom in 774 (Kingdom of the Lombards page: 'Between 773 and 774 he invaded Italy'); Spoleto, granted to the Church in 774-776, fell to him in 776.

wars.name: Lambert I's seizure of Rome
wars.outcome: Lambert seized Rome in 877-878; the Council of Troyes confirmed his excommunication in 878.

wars.name: Arnulf's Italian campaigns
wars.outcome: Arnulf's forces defeated Guy at Bergamo in 894 and Guy died on the Taro; in 896 Arnulf took Rome and the pope deposed Lambert, but Arnulf's advance stalled after a stroke and Lambert was restored once Formosus died.

wars.name: Lambert and Berengar's partition of the kingdom
wars.outcome: The two met near Pavia in October-November 896 and split the kingdom at the Adda; Lambert held the rest until his death on 15 October 898.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line for the duchy; the territory is described by the old regions it covered.
